questions.question: To reduce your risk of a crash, you should:

options.text: Be visible to other drivers.
Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Always stay within a foot of another vehicle.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax on the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep the motorcycle straight. Brake gently on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When riding in fog, you should:

options.text: Use your high beam headlight.
Use your low beam headlight.
Use no lights.
Switch between low and high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are near.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected when wearing:

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed.
Boots with tall heels.
Leather gloves.
Shoes that end below the ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs. Boots or shoes should be tall and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Use low heels so they don't catch on foot pegs. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and improve your grip on the controls.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, you should:

options.text: Keep riding, as the wobble will likely correct itself.
Brake hard.
Close the throttle to slow down.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Move your weight as far forward and down as you can. Pull off the road as soon as possible to fix the problem.

questions.question: An experienced rider:

options.text: Changes lane position as road and traffic conditions change.
Stays in one part of the lane at all times.
Weaves within the lane to be more visible.
Travels only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes lane position as road and traffic conditions change.
questions.explanation: A motorcyclist has three lane position choices. Pick the safest position based on current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: The effects of marijuana can last for:

options.text: No more than 15 minutes.
About one hour.
About two hours.
More than six hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: More than six hours.
questions.explanation: When smoked, marijuana affects the user within minutes and effects last two to four hours. When eaten, it takes over an hour to start working, but effects can last more than six hours.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, you should ride:

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Adjust your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Keep your eyes focused close to the front of the motorcycle.
Look through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.
Speed up before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo:

options.text: Acceleration takes less time, but stopping takes more time.
Both acceleration and stopping take more time.
Acceleration takes more time, but stopping takes less time.
Both acceleration and stopping take less time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both acceleration and stopping take more time.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo slows both acceleration and stopping compared to riding alone.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Come to a complete stop.
Speed up to create distance between you and the tailgater.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up can make things more dangerous by causing them to tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: If one rider in a group wants to ride faster than the others, what should the group do?

options.text: Let the rider go ahead and meet up at a designated spot later.
Speed up to keep up with that rider.
Split up and have every rider travel at their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the rider go ahead and meet up at a designated spot later.
questions.explanation: If one member of a group wants to ride faster than the others, let them go ahead of the group. Plan to meet at a designated spot later.

questions.question: If one of your tires goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Increase throttle.
Hold the handle grips loosely.
Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Speed up to exit the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If one tire goes flat while riding, ease off the throttle and stay in a straight line as you slow down. If you must brake, gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: Which colors help riders be seen best?

options.text: Orange and red.
Green and blue.
Purple and gold.
Black and white.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange and red.
questions.explanation: To be visible to other drivers, wear bright clothing in orange, red, yellow, or green.

questions.question: Why is riding directly beside another vehicle dangerous?

options.text: You may have trouble reaching a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It prevents other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding beside another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in their blind spot. The driver may move into your lane without seeing you. The vehicle also blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Provide a good view of the shoulder.
Provide a poor view of road hazards.
Invite others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position so you can see others and they can see you. Avoid riding in another driver's blind spot.

questions.question: Which is not a good choice when picking clothes for riding?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely.
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles.
Leather gloves.
A baseball cap to cover your hair.

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair.
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles, and durable gloves. A baseball cap does not provide the protection you need.

questions.question: The front brake is:

options.text: Safe if used properly.
Safe even if used improperly.
Only for use if the rear brake fails.
Not to be used regularly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safe if used properly.
questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used correctly. It is more powerful than the rear brake and provides most of your stopping power.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Slow or stop.
Left turn.
Right turn.
Backing up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn.
questions.explanation: You can use hand signals instead of or along with turn signals. A left arm extended straight out to the left means you plan to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: What is the best sitting position when riding?

options.text: Your arms hold you up.
You can easily reach the controls.
Your arms are straight when holding the handgrips.
Your knees are away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can easily reach the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit in a position that lets you use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Reach the handgrips without stretching. Your arms should be slightly bent. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.

questions.question: After a motorcycle helmet is in a crash, you should:

options.text: Look it over carefully.
Get a new one.
Give it to another rider.
Put a new chinstrap on it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a new one.
questions.explanation: Get a new helmet after a crash. Do not use the old one again.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Only a front brake.
Only a rear brake.
Brakes on both the front and rear.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes on both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes. One brake works the front wheel and one works the rear wheel.

questions.question: You should leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead when:

options.text: The road is dry.
Riding conditions are normal.
The road is wet.
You can see through the vehicle in front.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is wet.
questions.explanation: Leave more space when your motorcycle needs a longer distance to stop. Also increase your distance in heavy traffic or when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Kick the dog away.
Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Swerve around the dog.
Slow down as you approach, then speed up and pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach, then speed up and pass.
questions.explanation: Dogs are often attracted to motorcycles. If chased, slow down and approach the dog calmly. Then speed up and ride away from it.

questions.question: When riding on rough surfaces, you should:

options.text: Grip the handlebars loosely so they can move.
Grip the handlebars firmly to stay in control.
Use full throttle to get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet so it does not slip down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly to stay in control.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars tightly on rough surfaces. This keeps your motorcycle steady and helps you steer safely.
